newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH INDUSTRY UNION SEES CZK 200BLN '97 TRADE GAP.
newsitem.headline: CZECH INDUSTRY UNION SEES CZK 200BLN '97 TRADE GAP.

text.p: The Czech Union of Industry and Transport on Monday forecast the country's foreign trade deficit to widen to 200 billion crowns in 1997, and warned that the trend will not change unless the government takes action.

The union's president, Stepan Popovic, told a news conference that more extensive government support for exports, favourable write-off conditions, and more control over illegal and dumping imports was needed to turn the tide.
"I cannot imagine a turning point (in the development of trade) unless the government acts," Popovic said.
The Czech Republic posted a record 160.3 billion crown trade shortfall for 1996.
Popovic said the union was not calling for any radical measures, but said actions like a currency devaluation would logically have to follow at some point if nothing is done.

Popovic said the country's foreign exchange reserves, at $12.6 billion in November, were the last resource to tap to pay for imports after since the capital account can no longer cover the trade gap. The balance of payments showed a $1.06 billion deficit in the first nine months of 1996.

The Czech Statistical Bureau has forecast the trade deficit could reach 215 billion in 1997. Government officials have said they believe the dynamics of the deficit increase would stabilise by the end of this year.
